name: Wheel and Dog
description: A wheel that bows two melody strings and three drones without end, with a loose bridge that barks each time the wheel jerks.

params.name: Speed
params.description: How many times a second the wheel turns. The accents come round with it, and a faster wheel bows a little harder and brighter.

params.name: Spin
params.description: How long the wheel takes to come up to speed at the first key and to stop after the last. The accents stretch out as it slows.

params.name: Accents
params.description: How many times the hand pushes the wheel in one turn. With none it turns evenly and the strings hold still.

params.name: Pattern
params.description: How the pushes lie in the turn: evenly, every second one late, or the first one stronger than the rest.

params.name: Depth
params.description: How far the wheel's speed jumps at each push. The strings swell with it, and a jump over the dog's threshold makes it bark.

params.name: Dog
params.description: How loose the buzzing bridge stands under the third drone. Looser, it barks at smaller pushes, and louder and longer at large ones.

params.name: Split
params.description: Keys below this note hold the drones and play no melody. Keys from it up play the melody, and the drones sound under them.

params.name: Drone
params.description: The note the drones are tuned to. First key takes the lowest drone key held, and D until one is played on the turning wheel.

params.name: Tuning
params.description: Where the second and third drones stand over the low one, named in that order: an octave then the fifth over it, and so on.

params.name: Drones
params.description: Level of the two plain drones, the low one and the second one.

params.name: Third drone
params.description: Level of the third drone, the string that stands on the dog. The bark is made by this string, so it goes with it.

params.name: Detune
params.description: Tunes the third drone sharp. A touch makes a fifth over the low drones pure; more beats slowly against them and against the melody.

params.name: Melody
params.description: What the two melody strings play: both the newest key, the second one an octave lower, or the two newest keys held.

params.name: Tangents
params.description: Loudness of the wooden key stopping the melody string: a short knock of noise at each change of note.

params.name: Rosin
params.description: How hard the wheel grips the strings. Little rosin is thin and whispering, some is firm, and a lot is raw and rough.

params.name: Bow noise
params.description: Hiss of the wheel on the strings, let in with each slip of the string. It grows with the wheel's speed.

params.name: Brightness
params.description: How much of the upper overtones the strings give, from a covered hum to a bright edge.

params.name: Body
params.description: Blend from the bare strings to the wooden box they stand on, which takes off the lowest and highest tones and adds nasal middle resonances.

params.name: Spread
params.description: Places the five strings across the stereo field. At zero all of them sit in the centre.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when it is turned far up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit after the hurdy-gurdy: a wheel that bows melody strings, drones and one drone that stands on a loose, buzzing bridge. A signal model, with no sample and no measurement of an instrument in it. Each string is the ramp and slip of a string under a steady bow, band-limited at twice the sample rate, shaped by a low-pass and a shelf; there is no waveguide and no friction law, so nothing in it can go unstable or out of tune. Rosin moves a second slip in the period (little: it takes out the fundamental; much: it narrows the ramp) and adds uneven slips and drive. The wheel is an even clock with pushes on it; the jerk is the time derivative of the bow's speed and is what opens the dog; the bark is a one-sided contact on the third drone's own motion, then three resonances, a short diffuser for the bridge and its board and a ceiling, all at twice the rate. Choices and not measurements: the 22 ms rise of a push and its cubic fall, the dog's threshold law and its 90 ms chatter, the bridge's three resonances, the seven body resonances a side, the second slips' places, the lean of one melody string on the other and of either on a drone of its own note (six cents at most), every level. Simplified: no sympathetic strings, the strings do not move the bridge for each other but for those leans, the wheel is round but for 2 % of level a turn, the dog stands under the third drone alone, tangents are a burst of noise. Equal-tempered intervals on a tonic at A = 440 Hz unless it is taken from a key. Nobody has listened to it.
